subsystems.name: Pigment micro-capsules
subsystems.role: contain charged pigment particles that move under an electric field to change colour.

subsystems.name: Electrode array
subsystems.role: apply local electric fields to move pigment within each capsule.

subsystems.name: Control electronics
subsystems.role: receive wireless commands and drive voltages to the electrode array.

subsystems.name: Power source
subsystems.role: supply power to the electronics and electrode array.

subsystems.name: Biocompatible encapsulation
subsystems.role: protect the implant from body fluids and prevent immune rejection.

subsystems.name: External controller
subsystems.role: user interface to select patterns and send commands.

buildSteps.title: Design pixel layout
buildSteps.detail: Define the grid of colour cells and the electrode pattern needed to address each one independently.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate micro-capsules
buildSteps.detail: Emulsify charged pigment particles in a dielectric fluid and encapsulate them in polymer shells a few tens of micrometres across.

buildSteps.title: Build flexible electrode array
buildSteps.detail: Deposit conductive traces on a flexible polyimide substrate, then pattern and insulate them so each capsule has its own electrodes.

buildSteps.title: Integrate control electronics
buildSteps.detail: Assemble the microcontroller, wireless receiver, driver circuits and power source on a flexible circuit board.

buildSteps.title: Encapsulate the device
buildSteps.detail: Coat the whole implant with a thin, flexible, biocompatible barrier that keeps out water and ions for years.

buildSteps.title: Implant under the skin
buildSteps.detail: Place the device in a shallow sub-dermal pocket through a small incision, in a procedure similar to inserting a contraceptive implant.

buildSteps.title: Pair and calibrate
buildSteps.detail: Link the implant to a smartphone app and calibrate the voltage-to-colour response for each capsule.

buildSteps.title: Operate
buildSteps.detail: The user selects a pattern; the app sends commands; the electronics apply voltages that move pigment and change the skin's appearance.

prerequisites.why: proven in e-readers; provides the basic mechanism of moving charged pigment with an electric field.
implantable devices exist, but thin, flexible, large-area arrays that survive for decades in the body are still in research.

prerequisites.tech: Wireless power and data for implants
prerequisites.why: inductive links and radio telemetry are used in medical devices, but miniaturisation and efficiency for a large skin-area implant need work.
pacemakers are sealed in rigid titanium, but flexible implants need coatings that resist fibrosis and moisture for many years.
controlling the implant by thought would require a high-bandwidth brain-computer interface, which is not yet clinically available.

pathway.milestone: lab research on electrochromic and electrophoretic materials for skin
pathway.unlocks: proof of principle that colour can be changed under the skin.

pathway.milestone: flexible, wirelessly controlled implants tested in animals for months
pathway.unlocks: long-term biocompatibility and stable colour-change data.

pathway.milestone: first human trials for medical applications such as skin camouflage for burns or vitiligo
pathway.unlocks: a regulatory path and clinical refinement.
commercial products for dynamic appearance change.

pathway.milestone: integration with neural interfaces for thought control
